issues.description: Template class GroverTwoQubitWithoutAuxiliaryQubit has an inconsistent attribute name for the query register: it creates self._query_register but later (immediately) constructs the QuantumCircuit using self.query_register (which does not exist). This naming mismatch will raise an AttributeError/NameError and prevents students from instantiating or using the template as-is. The solution repository uses the attribute name self.query_register consistently.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute name consistent in the template. Replace self._query_register with self.query_register (or vice versa) and ensure the same attribute is used when constructing the QuantumCircuit. For example: self.query_register = QuantumRegister(self.number_of_qubits_query_register) and then self.qc = QuantumCircuit(self.query_register). This matches the solution and the exercise description.

issues.description: Constructor in the template uses a different attribute name for the query register than the rest of the template and the solution. The template sets self._query_register = QuantumRegister(...) but immediately uses self.query_register when building the QuantumCircuit. The problem statement and the solution use the identifier query_register. This mismatch creates a mapping/confusion for students (and will cause an AttributeError if executed) since the template's constructor does not define self.query_register consistently with the rest of the code and with the problem description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's constructor use the same identifier as the problem statement and solution. Replace self._query_register = QuantumRegister(...) with self.query_register = QuantumRegister(...) (and then use self.query_register when constructing the QuantumCircuit), or else consistently use the _query_register name everywhere in the file. Aligning the template to use query_register will remove the unexpected mismatch and match the solution and problem text.
